## What happens

This contract checks SP1 Groth16 proofs with the BN254 pairing. A bridge host on Ethereum accepts Polkadot consensus updates proven through it. A quantum computer can find the setup secret and pass a false update; the router's ECDSA route is a separate weakness.

## Evidence

- [verifyProof](https://etherscan.io/address/0x70303aa3434e13b64f150ce72bad43e13c8ed186#code) ends in a BN254 pairing check of the Groth16 proof.
- The [host](https://etherscan.io/address/0x620128e2b19193d6bd244a3ac8d3bba0541b19c3)'s consensus client routes SP1 proofs to a verifier that calls this address.
- The [host manager](https://etherscan.io/address/0x712515887e0dff042530a120dca9e8a3c90178a5) sets the host's consensus client for its 2-of-2 Safe, or for governance relayed by admin key 0xd150….

## Reviewer notes

### Mechanism

SP1Verifier.verifyProof (SP1VerifierGroth16.sol 51-81) checks the selector, exit code and vk root, then calls this.verifyProof (Groth16Verifier.sol 519+), which runs the BN254 pairing precompile 0x08 (line 557; the pairing at line 500 belongs to verifyCompressedProof, which is never called). At block 26,438,999 the host 0x620128e2's consensusClient() is router 0x64094bb4, whose sp1Beefy() is 0x3683cd18, whose verifier() is this address. A false proof, made with the trusted-setup secret, would let a false consensus update through; messages proven against it are then delivered to bridge applications. Only the host manager 0x71251588 can call the host's updateHostParams (which carries consensusClient). The manager does so for its owner, a 2-of-2 Safe, and in onAccept for a SetHostParams request from the Hyperbridge chain POLKADOT-3367 delivered with the admin key 0xd15007f5 (a plain key) as relayer, with no Safe signature. Apps on the host, such as IntentGatewayV2 0xae041f7b (host() = this host, 13.39 USDC), act on delivered messages.

### Checks

- Header facts: this address alone, at block 26,438,999.
- Ruled out: An admin on this verifier: none; it is not a proxy and has no owner (tool facts).
- Ruled out: Retired verifier: the host's live consensus path reaches this address at the block (calls client, router, beefy).
- Ruled out: The router also accepts BEEFY updates through an ECDSA client at 0xaec95085 whose code calls the ecrecover precompile (ecdsa-recover), checked against the host's stored authority set of 500 (authority-set). So the authorities sign with secp256k1 keys, and a quantum attacker who recovers two thirds of them can sign a false update that an honest SP1 proof or the ECDSA path accepts. That the off-chain SP1 program proves these same BEEFY ECDSA signatures is inferred from the shared trusted state, not read from the program.
- Ruled out: No path to change the client: the Safe through the host manager (mgrok, mgrfwd) and Hyperbridge governance through the manager's onAccept (gov-ok; other relayer or source chain refused: gov-other, gov-src).
- Ruled out: Whose money: the verifier holds $0; IntentGatewayV2, an app of this host, holds 13.39 USDC (gw-host, gw-usdc). Mint power over Hyperbridge-bridged tokens was not measured, so whose stays unset.

### Questions

- What a forged consensus update could mint or release behind the host is not measured: apps such as IntentGatewayV2 also check their own relayer, so the exposure is per app.
